items.title: Suns To Bring Back Haywood Highsmith
items.summary: Haywood Highsmith will re-sign with the Suns, league sources tell Michael Scotto of HoopsHype (Twitter link). It will be a one-year contract, agent Jerry Dianis confirms to ESPN’s Shams Charania (Twitter link). The veteran forward was waived last Wednesday after spending just a few months with the team, and he became a free agent after clearing waivers on Friday. He held a $1MM guarantee on his $3,018,158 contract for the upcoming season. Highsmith missed most of last season after undergoing surgery on a torn meniscus in his right knee last August and suffering a setback in his rehab in October. He signed a two-year, minimum-salary contract with Phoenix in February and appeared in seven regular season games and two playoff contests. Highsmith is likely getting another minimum-salary deal. The details of his new deal aren’t yet known, but if it’s non-guaranteed and includes Exhibit 9…

items.summary: Reaching an agreement to trade Dennis Schröder to Charlotte last week hasn’t changed the Cavaliers‘ plans to find a new home for Max Strus, Marc Stein of The Stein Line reports (subscription required). League sources tell Stein that Cleveland is still searching for a taker for Strus, who has a $16.7MM expiring contract for 2026/27. The Cavs saved roughly $6.8MM in the Schröder deal by swapping his $14.8MM salary for Tre Mann‘s $8MM figure. items.title: And-Ones: D’Antoni, Buss Brothers, Hartenstein, Hall Of Famers
items.summary: Mike D’Antoni was inducted into the Hall of Fame this weekend as part of the 2026 class. He knows that the primary reason he’s getting in is the philosophical change in the league that he helped usher in when he brought the “Seven Seconds or Less” philosophy over from his coaching days in Italy, ESPN’s Dave McMenamin writes. While D’Antoni’s Suns’ up-and-down, free-flowing offense influenced the way that teams play today, he still regrets that he didn’t push the style even further, closer to what it has become today. “Because we were first to go through the door, first of all, you take a lot of bullets. And … it makes you hesitate. We didn’t go as far as we could have pushed the envelope back then because we didn’t know,” D’Antoni said. “We’d shoot 30-something threes and we’re going, ‘Is that too many? items.summary: Dereck Lively II has undergone three foot surgeries in the last year as he works to try to get healthy for the upcoming season, and he still has more work to do. Mavericks general manager Mike Schmitz recently expressed confidence in the young center’s approach to his rehab process, according to Grant Afseth of the Dallas Hoops Journal. “[Lively] has been working his tail off. He’s in the facility constantly, completely locked into everything we’re doing and doing everything in his power to be his best self,” Schmitz said. “Really, really proud of just the approach he’s taken and his mentality, his voice. items.title: Sixers Adding Tommy Balcetis To Front Office
items.summary: The Sixers are hiring Tommy Balcetis as their new head of basketball intelligence, analytics and innovation, reports Michael Scotto of HoopsHype (via Twitter). The veteran NBA executive spent 12 years with the Nuggets from 2013-2025, earning multiple promotions in Denver’s front office. The Nuggets decided not to retain him in June 2025 after his contract expired. Balcetis was initially hired as Denver’s basketball analytics manager and worked his way up the organization from there, earning the title of director of strategy and analytics, then VP of basketball strategy and analytics. In 2020, he was promoted to assistant general manager, his last role with the organization. After parting ways with the Nuggets, Balcetis spent the 2025/26 season in his native Lithuania as Zalgiris Kaunas’ head of innovations.
